More at {{l|en|rural}}. {{doublet|en|Raum}}, a surname from German. {{col-bottom}} The word superficially appears to be an exception to the {{w|Great Vowel Shift}}, which might have produced the pronunciation {{IPAchar|/ɹaʊm/}}, but the retention of Middle English {{IPAchar|/uː/}} before {{IPAchar|/m/}} is regular. In fact, {{IPAchar|/aʊ/}} does not occur before non-[[coronal]] consonants in Standard Modern English native vocabulary. Some dialects did undergo diphthongization in such a position and the pronunciation {{IPAchar|/ɹaʊm/}} occurs, for example, in [[Lancashire]].Orton and Halliday, ''Survey of English Dialects Vol. 1 Basic Material Six Northern Counties and Man Part 2'' ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|roome||obsolete}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[space|Space]] for something, or to carry out an activity. {{defdate|from 10th c.}} #: {{ux|en|We haven't got enough '''room''' in here for that large wardrobe.}} #: {{ux|en|These seats give us plenty of '''room''' to stretch our legs.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|author=Jonathan Franklin|journal=The Guardian|date=27 Aug 2010 |passage=He explains they have enough '''room''' to stand and lie down, points out the "little cup to brush our teeth", and the place where they pray.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable|figuratively}} [[opportunity|Opportunity]] or [[scope]] (for something, or to do something). #: {{ux|en|The law is perfectly clear. ==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Cup of tea, Scotland.jpg|thumb|alt=An orange tea in a teacup|right|A cup of '''tea''' in Scotland.]]
[[File:Names for tea.png|alt=A world map in grey with blue and red dots|thumb|Names like ''cha'' in red, names like ''tea'' in blue, and other names in grey]]

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=drink|:bor|nl:thee}}
First appears c. 1655, in the English translation {{w|Álvaro Semedo}}’s writings. From {{bor|en|nl|thee}}, from {{der|en|nan-hbl|茶|tr=tê}} ({{w|Amoy dialect}}), from {{der|en|och|-}}, ultimately from {{der|en|sit-pro|*s-la||leaf, tea}}. Introduced to English and other Western European languages by the {{w|Dutch East India Company}}, who sourced their tea in {{w|Amoy}}; compare {{cog|ms|teh}} along the same trade route. {{doublet|en|chai|cha}} (and, distantly, the first element of {{m|en|lahpet}}), from same Proto-Sino-Tibetan root; see discussion of cognates.

{{box-top|Cognates}}
The word for “tea” in many languages is of Sinitic origin (due to China being the origin of the plant), and thus there are many cognates; see [[#Translations|translations]]. These are from one of two proximate sources, reflected in the phonological shape: forms with a stop (e.g. {{IPAchar|/t/}}) are derived from Min Nan ''tê'', while forms with an affricate (e.g. {{IPAchar|/tʃ/}}) are derived from other Sinitic languages, like Mandarin ''chá'' or Cantonese ''caa4'' (all written as {{zh-l|*茶}}). Different languages borrowed one or the other form (specific language and point in time varied), reflecting trade ties, generally Min Nan ''tê'' if by ocean trade from Fujian, Cantonese ''caa4'' if by ocean trade from Guangdong, or northern Chinese ''chá'' if by overland trade or by ocean trade from India.<ref>''The World Atlas of Language Structures Online,'' “[http://wals.info/feature/138 Chapter 138: Tea]”, by Östen Dahl</ref>

Thus Western and Northern European languages borrowed ''tê'' (with the exception of Portuguese, which uses {{m|pt|chá}}; despite being by ocean trade, their source was in {{w|Macao}}, not Amoy), while ''chá'' borrowings are used over a very large geographical area of Eurasia and Africa: Southern and Eastern Europe, and on through Turkish, Arabic, North and East Africa, Persian, Central Asian, and Indic languages. In Europe the ''tê''/''chá'' line is Italian/Slovene, Hungarian/Romanian, German/Czech, Polish/Ukrainian, Baltics/Russian, Finnish/Karelian, Northern Sami/Inari Sami. ''tê'' was also borrowed in European trade stops in Southern India and coastal Africa, though ''chá'' borrowings are otherwise more prevalent in these regions, via Arabic or Indic, due to earlier trade. The situation in Southeast Asia is complex due to multiple influences, and some languages borrowed both forms, such as Malay {{m|ms|teh}} and {{m|ms|ca}}.
{{box-bottom}}

{{senseno|en|information, especially gossip|uc=1}} (“information, especially gossip”) may be originally from ''T'' standing for {{m|en|truth}}, which evolved into ''tea''. An alternative explanation dates back to gay African-American culture in the 1970s and alludes to women gossiping over afternoon tea.<ref name="npr">{{cite-web |en |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/08/27/g-s1-85471/whats-tea-no-seriously-whats-tea |title=What's tea? No, seriously. What's 'tea'? |work={{w|All Things Considered}} |publisher={{w|NPR}} |date=2025-08-27 |accessdate=2025-08-28 |first=Alana |last=Wise|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260203070018/https://www.npr.org/2025/08/27/g-s1-85471/whats-tea-no-seriously-whats-tea|archivedate=3 February 2026}}</ref>

#: {{ux|en|She is a brilliant academic, but completely impractical around the '''house'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'll job out the plumbing work on the '''house'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Marshall Squire's Daughter|III
|passage=The big '''houses''', and there are a good many of them, lie for the most part in what may be called by courtesy the valleys. You catch a glimpse of them sometimes at a little distance from the [railway] line, which seems to have shown some ingenuity in avoiding them,{{nb...}}.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage=Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path {{nb...}}. It twisted and turned,{{...}}and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn. # {{senseid|en|building for single household residence}} A building intended to contain a single household, as opposed to an [[apartment]] or [[condominium]] or building containing these.

#* {{RQ:KJV|Acts|10|2|passage=one that feared God with all his '''house'''}}

#: {{ux|en|On arriving at the zoo, we immediately headed for the [[monkey house|monkey '''house''']].}}
## {{senseid|en|place of business, company, organization}} A place of [[business]]; a company or organisation, especially a [[printing press]], a [[publishing]] company, or a [[couturier]]. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|A small publishing '''house''' would have a contract with an independent fulfillment '''house'''.}}
##* {{RQ:Dickens Little Dorrit|passage=I have a good banker in this city, but I would not wish to draw upon the '''house''' until the time when I shall draw for a round sum.}}
## {{senseid|en|place of public accommodation or entertainment}} A place of public accommodation or entertainment, especially a [[public house]], an [[inn]], a [[restaurant]], a [[theatre]], or a [[casino]]; or the management thereof. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|One more, sir, then I'll have to stop serving you – rules of the '''house''', I'm afraid.}}
##: {{ux|en|The '''house''' always wins.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1964|title=Northwest Ohio Quarterly|volume=36|page=185|passage=The farce comedy which followed, ''When We're Married'' by Charles Burnham, was heartily praised, with the character man singled out for special extollation. The production filled the '''house'''.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=27 Aug 77|volume=5|number=8|journal=Gay Community News|page=9|author=Steve Savage;Susan "Suki" Eagan|title=Everything You Wanted to Know About Suki, But Were Too Distracted In Chaps to Ask Her|text=Frazier and Gary worked for me for free — for six months — they didn't take any money from the '''house'''. They worked for tips.}}
## {{lb|en|historical}} A [[workhouse]].
##* {{quote-book|en|title=Reports from the Commissioners|passage=To this the pauper replied that he did not want that, and that rather than be sent to the '''house''' he would look out for work.|year=1834|author=Great Britain. Parliament. House of Commons|page=169|volume=29}}
# The audience for a live theatrical or similar performance. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|After her swan-song, there wasn't a dry eye in the '''house'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Orczy Miss Elliott|story=The Affair at the Novelty Theatre|chapter=2|passage=Miss Phyllis Morgan, as the hapless heroine dressed in the shabbiest of clothes, appears in the midst of a gay and giddy throng; she apostrophises all and sundry there, including the villain, and has a magnificent scene which always brings down the '''house''', and nightly adds to her histrionic laurels.}}
# {{senseid|en|legislative body or building thereof}} {{lb|en|politics}} A building where a deliberative assembly meets; whence the assembly itself, particularly a component of a [[legislature]]. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|The petition was so ridiculous that the '''house''' rejected it after minimal debate.}}
# A [[dynasty]]; a family with its [[ancestor]]s and [[descendant]]s, especially a royal or noble one. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|A curse lay upon the '''House''' of Atreus.}}
# {{lb|en|metaphorical}} A place of [[rest]] or [[repose]]. {{defdate|from 9th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Jonson Every Man in His Humour|text=Like a pestilence, it doth infect / The '''houses''' of the brain.}}
#* {{RQ:Scott Lord of the Isles|text=Such hate was his, when his last breath / Renounced the peaceful '''house''' of death {{nb...}}.}}
# A [[grouping]] of [[schoolchildren]] for the purposes of competition in sports and other activities. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I was a member of Spenser '''house''' when I was at school.}}

#* {{quote-book|en|title=Religion and the Decline of Magic|passage=Since there was a limited number of planets, '''houses''' and signs of the zodiac, the astrologers tended to reduce human potentialities to a set of fixed types and to postulate only a limited number of possible variations.|year=1971|author=[[w:en:Keith Thomas (historian)|Sir Keith Vivian Thomas]]|page=313|isbn=978-0-14-013744-6|year_published=2012|publisher=[[w:en:Folio Society|The Folio Society]]}}

=====Usage notes=====
* ''Milk'' is often taken to mean [[cow's milk]] when the context makes that meaning certain or likely.
* ''Milk'' is often held to mean solely mammary milk from {{l|en|animal|animals|id=Q729}} (including humans), rather than any other liquid that mimics it.
** Following a [[European Union]] (EU) court ruling in 2017, the term ''milk'' cannot legally be used to market purely plant-based products ({{senseno|en|white liquid from a vegetable source}}) in the EU.<ref>{{cite-web|url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:62016CJ0422&from=EN|date=14 June 2017|work=EUR-Lex|title=Judgment of the Court (Seventh Chamber) of 14 June 2017|passage=The term ‘milk’ shall mean exclusively the normal mammary secretion obtained from one or more milkings without either addition thereto or extraction therefrom.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251021114743/https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A62016CJ0422&from=EN|archivedate=21 October 2025}}</ref>
